subject: Re: DataQuarry vendor exit — packaging options and fallback economics
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@dataquarry.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@dataquarry.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring replacement and pricing alignment

Karthik —

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. We ran a quick executive review and DataQuarry is actively evaluating a vendor replacement due to an aggressive price increase from our incumbent. Before we move further down that path, procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a packaged alternative that accomplishes two things:

- Match the incumbent's list economics for the first 12 months (they want a direct price match)
- Offer an ops-friendly migration path (pilot + migration credits + clear rollback)

I attached our RFP (DataQuarry_RFP_v3.pdf) for context. Key constraints: 1) strict uptime SLA for inference at the edge, 2) encrypted KV cache requirement, and 3) a two-week pilot with a non-production dataset.

Can you confirm if a price-match + migration credit structure is plausible from Redwood, or if your packaging leans toward bundle discounts or seat-based prepay? Happy to do a short call — procurement is moving fast.

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Head of Cloud Platform
DataQuarry Inc.
[attachment: DataQuarry_RFP_v3.pdf (PDF)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@dataquarry.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement and pricing alignment

Sara —

Appreciate the RFP and context. We can absolutely discuss a price-match approach — common pattern is a staged match (12 months list parity) paired with a migration credit to offset early switching costs and an operations-focused pilot. I summarized a pragmatic path in the attached one-pager (DQ_Redwood_Summary.pdf).

High level options we typically propose:

1) Straight match + migration credit: 12 months list-price match, one-time onboarding credit (covers up to 60% of migration tooling / egress), 90-day SLA uplift window.
2) Bundle-first: 12-month committed bundle with deeper unit pricing and phased consumption true-up; smaller upfront credit but lower run rate.
3) Pilot-first: 8-week pilot free, then apply pilot credits to first invoice if you convert.

Lauren (SE) and Monica (CS) are looped for technical fit and onboarding cost estimates. Can we lock a 30m on Tuesday 10/27? I can bring a brief term-sheet and an ops checklist.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: DQ_Redwood_Summary.pdf (PDF)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: DataQuarry — inputs on packaging and SLA

Karthik / Monica —

Quick notes after scanning the RFP and Karthik's summary:

- Edge SLA: we can support sub-100ms p95 on their target instance types; need to confirm which HW they run in prod. If they use mixed GPU fleets, offer a fallback model variant to hit cost objectives.
- KV cache encryption: supported via customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) — requires the Private deployment path for full control; however, Dedicated with VPC peering can meet procurement needs if they accept CMK/partial control.
- Pilot: 2-week pilot with sample dataset is doable but ops will want a 4-week window for realistic traffic; recommend we phrase as "2-week technical validation + 2-week performance ramp".

Packaging recommendation: propose Option 1 (Match + onboarding credit) as primary. Option 2 (bundle) can be a fallback if they insist on guaranteed unit economics in perpetuity. For the migration credit, suggest a $50k capped credit tied to milestones (pilot complete, production go-live, data egress completed).

I'll draft a short commercial play (terms + milestone triggers) and loop Markus for legal/approval on the cap.

-Lauren
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: DataQuarry — inputs on packaging and SLA

Karthik / Lauren —

Agree with the $50k migration credit as a sensible cap for the usual lift. A couple of operational questions procurement will ask:

- Does Redwood provide a rollback / escape window with preserved data access if they decide to revert to incumbent? We typically include an egress assistance addendum (discounted egress for 30 days + transfer scripts).
- Billing cadence: procurement prefers monthly consumption billing for the first 6 months rather than upfront prepay. If we do a price match, we should align the billing model to their preference or at least offer a monthly true-up clause.

I'll prepare a short onboarding-cost worksheet (internal) to justify the $50k cap and estimate our SE/CS hours. If legal needs a precedent, Markus — can you confirm whether we have approval to sign a 12-month list-match clause with a 30-day terminal notice?

Thanks,
Monica
Principal Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@dataquarry.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement and pricing alignment — proposal attached

Sara —

Thanks again for the RFP and for the quick review. Based on your ask and our internal scoping, attached is a short term-sheet (matching-term-sheet.docx) and the proposed commercial path: 

Proposal (summary):
- 12 months list-price parity on equivalent units (price-match)
- $50,000 migration credit (milestone-based: pilot complete, go-live, post-migration validation)
- 2-week technical validation + 2-week performance ramp pilot (pilot credits apply to first invoice on conversion)
- Monthly consumption billing for first 6 months with a conversion true-up if you opt for annual bundle thereafter
- Egress assistance addendum: discounted egress rates for 30 days + transfer scripts for rollback

Operational notes: Private deployment recommended for strict CMK/KV encryption control; Dedicated with VPC peering is acceptable if procurement is comfortable with managed CMK options (we included both paths in the term-sheet).

Next steps: if this aligns, I can run a short legal precedent check with Markus and send a DocuSign for an LOI + pilot SOW. Would Tuesday 10/29 at 11am PT work for a 30m call to finalize pilot scope?

Link to LOI (preview): https://www.docusign.com/confirm/abc123-example

Best,
Karthik Iyer
